title: Why the $9.99 trick still works on you

vo.text: $9.99 is a lie your brain believes.
Your brain reads prices left to right — and stops early. The first digit sets the anchor.
Step one. Shoppers were shown a shirt at $34, then at $39.
The $39 shirt sold 24 percent more. Higher price. More sales.
Step two. Prices ending in nine beat round prices in 60 percent of tests.
Step three. Drop the 9 to a 7 — $9.97 — and the effect barely moves. It was never about the 9.
It's the left digit. Your brain banks the 9 dollars and rounds the rest to zero.
So the trick isn't 99 cents. It's one cent — the one that moves the first number.
Which is why $9.99 is a lie your brain believes.
